Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

# Summary of Political Manifesto 2024

## Economic Policy

The manifesto emphasises economic stability following recent global challenges including the pandemic and international conflicts. Key economic claims include reduced inflation, rising real wages, and returning growth. The document outlines plans to reduce borrowing and debt while maintaining fiscal rules requiring public sector net debt to fall and borrowing to remain below 3% of GDP.

Business support measures include maintaining corporation tax rates, extending "full expensing" policies for investment, and supporting small businesses through rates relief and VAT threshold adjustments. Infrastructure investment totalling £36 billion is proposed for transport projects, including road maintenance, rail connectivity, and regional development.

## Taxation

The manifesto proposes cutting employee National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027, representing approximately £1,350 annually for average earners. Self-employed individuals would see their main National Insurance rate abolished entirely. A "Triple Lock Plus" would protect pensioners by ensuring both State Pension and tax-free allowances rise with the highest of inflation, earnings, or 2.5%.

Child Benefit reforms would move to a household-based system, with families retaining full benefits until combined income reaches £120,000. The document commits to not raising income tax, VAT, or Capital Gains Tax.

## Immigration and Border Control

The manifesto proposes a legally binding cap on migration, set annually through parliamentary vote, with numbers falling each year. Measures include removing illegal migrants, reforming asylum rules through international cooperation, and increasing visa fees. Salary thresholds for skilled workers have been raised to £38,700, and restrictions placed on dependants for students and care workers.

## Healthcare

NHS spending would increase above inflation annually, with plans for 92,000 additional nurses and 28,000 more doctors. Reforms include expanding pharmacy services, building diagnostic centres, and modernising GP surgeries. Mental health support would expand to all schools by 2030, with increased talking therapies and early support hubs.

## Housing

A target of 1.6 million homes is proposed, focusing on brownfield development and urban regeneration. First-time buyers would benefit from permanent Stamp Duty relief up to £425,000 and a new Help to Buy scheme. Leasehold reforms would cap ground rents and improve leaseholder protections.

## Defence and Security

Defence spending would increase to 2.5% of GDP by 2030, with investment in munitions production, technology modernisation, and continued support for international allies. The manifesto emphasises maintaining nuclear deterrent capabilities and strengthening cyber defences.

## Education and Skills

Proposals include mandatory National Service for 18-year-olds, offering either military or civic service options. Education reforms focus on the Advanced British Standard for 16-19 education, 100,000 additional apprenticeships, and mobile phone bans in schools. Special educational needs provision would expand with 60,000 additional school places.

## Environment and Energy

The manifesto commits to net zero by 2050 while emphasising energy security through continued North Sea oil and gas licensing, nuclear expansion including Small Modular Reactors, and trebled offshore wind capacity. Consumer protections include maintaining energy price caps and reducing green levies on household bills.

## Welfare Reform

Proposed changes include tightening disability benefit assessments, introducing stricter sanctions for long-term unemployed individuals, and accelerating Universal Credit rollout. The document projects £12 billion annual savings through reduced welfare claims and fraud prevention.

# Summary of 2024 Political Manifesto

This manifesto outlines a comprehensive policy platform focused on five key themes: economic fairness, public services, environmental protection, international relations, and democratic reform.

## Economic Policy

The document proposes responsible fiscal management while investing in renewable energy and home insulation to reduce energy bills and create jobs. Key economic measures include replacing business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy to support high streets, expanding apprenticeships, creating Lifelong Skills Grants for adult education, and reforming parental leave. The manifesto emphasises supporting small businesses, entrepreneurs, and addressing the cost-of-living crisis through energy efficiency programmes and careful economic management.

## Healthcare and Social Care

Healthcare proposals centre on guaranteeing GP appointments within seven days (24 hours for urgent cases), recruiting 8,000 additional GPs, and ensuring NHS dental access for emergency care. Mental health receives significant attention, with plans for community hubs and school-based mental health professionals. The manifesto proposes introducing free personal care based on need rather than ability to pay, creating a Royal College of Care Workers, and establishing a cross-party commission on sustainable social care funding. Unpaid carers would receive increased support including paid carer's leave and respite breaks.

## Education

Educational priorities include placing mental health professionals in every school, increasing per-pupil funding above inflation, providing tutoring guarantees for disadvantaged pupils, and reinstating maintenance grants for university students. Early years investment features prominently, with additional free hours for disadvantaged children and increased Early Years Pupil Premium funding.

## Environment

Environmental commitments include achieving net zero emissions by 2045, generating 90% of electricity from renewables by 2030, and implementing emergency home insulation programmes. The manifesto strongly emphasises ending sewage pollution through transforming water companies into public benefit entities, banning executive bonuses until pollution ends, and replacing the current water regulator. Nature protection targets include doubling protected areas, wildlife habitats, species abundance, and woodland cover by 2050.

## Housing

Housing proposals target building 380,000 homes annually, including 150,000 social homes, through new garden cities and community-led development. Renter protections include banning no-fault evictions and creating three-year default tenancies. The manifesto commits to ending rough sleeping and abolishing residential leasehold.

## Crime and Justice

Policing reforms focus on restoring community policing, guaranteeing investigation of all burglaries, and creating an Online Crime Agency. The manifesto proposes tackling court backlogs, improving prison rehabilitation, and better supporting domestic abuse survivors.

## Immigration and Asylum

Immigration policy would transfer work visa decisions from the Home Office to relevant departments, expand youth mobility schemes, and reverse income threshold increases for family visas. Asylum reforms include processing claims within three months, allowing asylum seekers to work after three months, and establishing safe legal routes while working with European authorities to combat trafficking.

## Democratic Reform

Constitutional changes include introducing proportional representation for elections, lowering voting age to 16, capping political donations, and reforming the House of Lords. The manifesto proposes enshrining the Ministerial Code in law and creating a federal constitution with strengthened devolution.

## International Relations

Foreign policy priorities include rebuilding European relationships through a four-stage roadmap toward closer integration, supporting Ukraine, returning international development spending to 0.7% of national income, and advocating for a ceasefire and two-state solution in the Israel-Gaza conflict. Defence commitments include reversing army cuts and increasing spending toward 2.5% of GDP while maintaining nuclear deterrence.
